title: Question before purchase about battle systems

posts.author: DatRpgGuy
posts.body:
I'm exploring a few engines to make my dream game, I have been playing around in Game Maker, Godot, Unreal. I know they can all do what I want, but I like the Idea of RPG maker because it makes some areas a lot simplier for me to do, areas that are not as important for the game I want to make.
How much flexibility do you have for a battle system?
I have envisioned a very complicated battle system, essentially a Turn based system based around criticals that does injuries and has tiers of damage. For example, a small cut on a hand, all the way up to a total removal of that hand, which will then also affect abilities that may use that hand.
Now apply similar system and damage tiers to different parts, eyes, head, neck, etc.
Also damage different critical based on damage type etc.
In theory there could be 100s if not in the 1000s of variables for any attack/defend action in the battle.
Is this something realistic for RPG Maker?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
First, the code for MV and MZ is completely open - so anything can be done, it just is a question of how much work it is - the more difference to a "default JRPG", the more work it will be.
older makers are more restricted, RM2K(3) and earlier don't even have script access while RMXP, RMVX and RMVXA are partially closed source and have some restrictions on what can be done.
Second, there are already a lot of different Battle Plugins available if you can't code yourself.
However I have not yet seen any plugin for that complex type of targeting areas.
It is doable, no question about that. With limited option it could even be implemented by states (if you work with dozens instead of thousands of variables).
That said, a system like you describe would have to be implemented from zero - but that would be neccessary in basically any engine, I don't think there is one that already uses such a system.
So it basically comes down to your experience in programming and which languages you have that experience in.
You also can hire someone else to do the coding (although your post count is too low to see the classified area for paid commissions), but for that to work you would have to put the entire system to paper first, and it would not be cheap.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
Without re-writing significant portions of battle engine code, you will not be able to create a system that allows a character to select which body parts they are aiming for on an enemy.  The rest can all be done with numbers, chances, and effects.  In RMMZ, the Visustella plugin suite is already equipped to do much of what you want... problem is it's obfuscated and you can barely customize it.
If you want to do this with minimal or no programming and are willing to adapt... gain a little more feature here... lose a little there,  MZ with VS plugins could be the way to go.  Otherwise, MV would allow fuller customization, less the targeting part, but with extra programming required.  Same goes for MZ without Visustella, except even more programming required to get what you want.  Don't forget that considerable thoughtfully balanced and play-tested data entry will be needed for your concept.
Creative compromises:
You could have individual skills that target specific locations, useable only under specific conditions, that have unique effects.  You can alter the critical hit dynamic many ways, but there is only one critical hit type by default, so you either elaborate conditionally on it, or adopt other mechanics in to it interactively.
Example:
You can have skills cause states and conditions that effect critical rate, critical resistance, and to some extent critical damage.  You can have skill damages that depend on or are magnified by the existence of specified states.  You can have successful critical hits give or remove various types of boost points which could be required for certain skills.  You can set up chain attacks that have to be performed in a successful sequence.  You can have skills which are inapplicable at the moment, be grayed out or not show at all.
In the end... you wont get exactly what you want, but you might be happier with the final results.  That said, anything can be programmed in RPG maker if you have the time, ability, money, and/or determination.

So in essence, the idea is a damage formula, that will determine the severity of a possible injury. Some moves will target specific body parts by default, other moves will be random target body part or a chosen target. I can't answer directly about what is currently in RPG maker, as I don't own a copy.
Robro33 said:
when you say that the parts are being injured, does the player select the different parts or does each skill only target a specific part? cause making something like "Eye Gouge" that deals damage to eyes is much easier implement than making a "Stab" skill that the player can use on target and then have to target a body part with.

Its kind of a hybrid I guess.
If you do a basic attack with a sword. You would have a % chance to do slash type damage, % chance to do pierce, and a % chance to do  blunt. Then after the type of damage is determined, either a random body part will be chosen to apply that damage, or a specific body part if you chose that to be your target.
Then, depending on severity of the hit, a critical table will be applied, that will cause specific status effects like blood loss, stun, removal of abilities, even death if the crit is strong enough.
Battles will end either through accumulating enough damage or a strong enough crit if to an area that can cause death. Like a pierce attack to an eye that is strong enough to hit their brain. Or a slash attack to a neck that will cause them to bleed out very quick or get decapitated.

how many parts and tiers are you thinking of having? My first suggestion would have been making each level of damage on each part its own state and using Turan's Eval Tags or Visustella skills and states plugin to manage applications, but if you end up with something like 20 parts and 5 tiers of damage youd ideally want a custom plugin to manage it imo.
Click to expand...
I envision a 5-10 tier based system on severity of the critical and the corresponding status effect because of that.
I do have a very complicated system already planed out that can target hands, arms, legs, eyes, neck, chest, and head. And different effects if the for damage types and crits to that area.
To add to my pierce example, a pierce has a higher chance to cause instant death to somethings eye, than a slash would. So there will be some tactical aspect to how you target parts with certain weapon types.
So for the eyes alone, using slash/pierce/crush damage tables. I currently have planned 21 different end results based on the crit. This is just end result. The formula itself could have upwards 10-15 Variables before you get a number to apply to a specific damage table. For example, how different attributes affect the attack and defense, extra attributes on the weapon, like some special weapons may have bonuses to critical tiers aka vorpal sword in DND, or some armors may have resistances to critical tiers or even damage types.

what exactly do you mean by this?
Click to expand...
A slash type attack will have a different damage and crit table than a blunt type, or a pierce.
Also, different elemental attacks will also have it's own corresponding damage/crit tables.
The damage formula will only determine that table to use, and the corresponding damage and/or status effect for a specific critical tier. If the target can be affected by that crit.
Robro33 said:
why do you see yourself needing all of these variables and what will you be using them for? if most of it is just storing body part status then you wouldnt need most if not any of them depending on how its all set up.
Click to expand...
This is the core design of my idea and game play. The battle system is the hook for the game. I'm trying to design a battle system that has a lot of variables to make it more tactical than traditional RPGs. Instead of using a grid like in a tactical rpg, the tactics come from the actually 1v1 fight instead of how you use positioning, you will use targeted attacks, or brute force, or maybe something else. There will be a leveling system, for the most part would be more like a chess match than simply kill as many as fast as possible. Average fight against a equal level threat should ideally, take 3-5 minutes, depending on level disparity this will shrink in favor of either you or your enemy.
I'm being a little intentionally vague on some details, but trying to give enough info to explain my idea.
In the time you might go through 10-20 fights in a traditional JRPG, this one you might have 2-4 fights. But the rewards and progression should be roughly the same for your time commitment.
I know I could do the system in a text based type rpg similar to older MUDs without too much difficulty, but I'm trying to make it more a visual representation with pixel art.
The plan with be a dragon warrior type view point, where the main focus will be your target, with visual representations real time damage and effects. Every critical status effect should be shown visually on your enemy in real time. In theory this will be easier to accomplish with the layering system in RPG maker.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
RPG Maker's strength compared to other engines is it has a lot of systems like the battle system prebuilt. The more you have to make your own plugins or write your own code the less reason there is to use it over its competitors.
You'll likely have to make the whole thing from scratch in another engine so it's just a question of how much work would modifying RPG Maker's battle system would save you compared to building it from the ground up.

One thing to be aware of is that the editor only supports having 8 enemies in a battle, so making them all separate body parts will limit how many simultaneous enemies you can have at any one time depending on how many parts they have (to the point where you may only be able to have one enemy total). There are plugins that allow you to break this limit, but it would still prevent you from using the editor itself to set up your battles.

I only plan on having 1v1 battles in the game, there might be a gauntlet where you go through many fights, but it'll always be 1v1.
